input.question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure if you're going to get a proper ELI5 answer to this: understanding why things run that fast requires understanding how computers are designed and the network architecture of the Internet - not exactly light reading. But to give more details about investors: yes, investment firms will pay out the nose for real estate as close to the stock exchange as possible, so that their trading servers will have as little lag as they can. Every last millisecond counts.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a big game together in a playground. You all have walkie-talkies so you can talk to each other and tell everyone what you are doing—like “I’m running to the swings!” or “I found a treasure!”

Now, imagine there are hundreds or even thousands of kids playing together at the same playground. It would be really hard to keep track of everyone and make sure everyone hears the right things at the right time.

But computers are super smart and really fast. The game has something like a big helper (called a “server”) that listens to everyone’s walkie-talkie at the same time. This helper quickly tells everyone else what each player is doing, so it looks like you are all playing together smoothly.

That’s how big online games like CoD or WoW work—they use super-fast computers to make sure everyone’s actions are shared quickly, so it feels like you’re all playing in the same place!
